subject: US Privacy Annex — deletion SLA & subprocessor emergency onboarding
messages:
From: Maya Brown <maya.brown@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Luke Chen <luke.chen@greenleafhealth.com>, procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: US privacy annex questions — deletion proof & subprocessors

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams are reviewing Redwood's standard DPA and a couple of items came up that we'd like to resolve before we move to contracting: 

1) Deletion SLA / Proof: For patient-like PII we need a documented deletion workflow plus an auditable receipt of deletion tied to the request id (we typically ask for a deletion confirmation that can be produced within 30 days). Can Redwood provide the workflow and a sample confirmation artifact?

2) Subprocessor emergency onboarding: GreenLeaf requires a commitment that any new subprocessors brought online for this account will be disclosed 30 days in advance, except in documented emergency scenarios. In emergencies, we need a post-notice within 7 days and the same contractual obligations extended to the subprocessors.

3) US-state transfer nuance: Several of our records are flagged for CA/VA residency. Can you confirm whether Redwood considers internal telemetry (e.g., model telemetry/usage logs) as "Service Provider" data or "Sale" category under CCPA/CPRA?

We attached our standard privacy annex for reference in the Drive link. If you can respond with examples and proposed redlines to the DPA by next Wednesday (28 Apr) that would be great.

Best,
Maya
Maya Brown
Senior Privacy Counsel, GreenLeaf Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Brown <maya.brown@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 12:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: US privacy annex questions — deletion proof & subprocessors

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear asks and for flagging the residency tags. High-level answers below; Marissa (legal) and Aditya (compliance/ops) are looped for specifics and attachments.

1) Deletion SLA / Proof: We treat account-level deletion requests as actionable operations. Workflow: customer submits deletion request (API/console + support ticket) -> ops validates scope -> deletion job scheduled (kv-cache + long-term storage scrub) -> post-run verification job compares record counts and produces a signed JSON confirmation including request id, timestamp, operator id, and scope. Typical turnaround: 7-30 days depending on retention category and backups. We can provide a sample signed confirmation artifact (we'll attach a redacted example).

2) Subprocessor emergency onboarding: Redwood's standard practice is 30-day notice for new subprocessors. For emergency onboarding we allow accelerated onboarding but we provide: (a) post-deployment notice within 7 days; (b) immediate contract flowdown obligations; (c) SOC2/HIPAA-equivalent evidence delivered within 30 days. We can add explicit language in the annex to bind these commitments.

3) Telemetry classification: By default, internal telemetry tied to billing/usage/observability is treated as "Service Provider" operational data and not a "sale". That said, if telemetry contains derived personal identifiers that GreenLeaf flags as CA-resident personal data, we can treat those as covered by the same controls as customer data and respect residency filtering. We will propose a clause that (i) classifies telemetry as service provider data, (ii) requires residency filters for CA-flagged records, and (iii) disallows onward sale.

Next steps: Aditya will attach the redlined DPA and a sample deletion confirmation. Marissa will propose specific language for the emergency subprocessor section. We'll return the materials by EOD Tue 28 Apr.

Regards,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: US privacy annex questions — deletion proof & subprocessors

Maya / Naomi —

Couple of proposed redlines to address GreenLeaf's asks (summary):

• Deletion confirmation artifact: add language that Redwood will provide a signed deletion confirmation JSON including request id, scope, timestamp, operator id, and hash of records deleted; retention of the confirmation artifact will be 3 years for audit purposes.

• Emergency subprocessors: add a clause that permits exceptions only where substantial operational risk or third-party failure would cause service outage, defined with examples (e.g., critical model repo vulnerability or cloud region outage). In such cases, Redwood will: (1) provide written notice within 48 hours of deployment; (2) provide a remediation plan and documented SOC2/HIPAA-equivalent evidence within 30 days; (3) allow GreenLeaf to request suspension of processing for affected data flows in a rolling 90-day remediation window.

• Residency enforcement: add a narrow residency filter obligation: Redwood will route CA-flagged records to region-specific processing and will not include CA-flagged PII in aggregate telemetry exports. We should offer operational controls for customers to opt-in to stricter isolation.

I will include the specific contract language in the redline. One ask for clarity: does GreenLeaf expect the deletion confirmation to include hashes of deleted objects, or a count + sample IDs? Hashes are better for proof without exposing dataset samples.

-M
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: US privacy annex questions — deletion proof & subprocessors

Maya — attaching the DPA redline and current subprocessor roster (see attachments). A few operational notes that may help your team assess timelines: 

• Deletion flow: there are three retention tiers in our infra — ephemeral (KV cache, auto-evict within 24h), short-term (tokenized request logs, 7–30 days), and archival (backups, up to 90 days by default). Our deletion job targets all tiers and interacts with snapshot restores; we flag backups for scheduled overwrite within retention windows. True irrecoverable deletion for archival backups can take up to 30 days depending on snapshot cycles.

• Proof artifact options:
  - Option A: Signed JSON with request id, deleted record count, SHA256 hashes for a provided sample of IDs (privacy-preserving), operator id, and timestamp.
  - Option B: Signed attest letter from Redwood Ops with a summary of steps taken and a CSV of redacted IDs.

• Subprocessor evidence: for any newly engaged infra subcontractor we can provide the contractual flowdown language and a SOC2 report. For emergency onboarding we can commit to the 7-day post-notice + 30-day SOC2 evidence timeline.

Deliverables: attached DPA_Draft_GreenLeaf_v2.pdf (redline) and subprocessor_list_2026Q1.csv. Please review and tell us preference for the proof artifact (Option A or B) and any stricter residency rules you require.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Compliance Operations, Redwood Inference

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. We reviewed the materials with our security and procurement partners. A few points: 

• We prefer Option A (signed JSON with sample hashes) as the deletion confirmation artifact — allows us to independently verify without sharing raw IDs.
• Emergency subprocessors: the 48-hour notice and 30-day SOC2 window are acceptable provided the DPA explicitly lists examples of emergency scenarios and includes the suspension right for impacted flows.
• Residency: GreenLeaf will accept region-specific processing for CA-flagged records, but requests that telemetry meant for product analytics be stripped of CA-flagged identifiers before any aggregate export.

Next step: procurement will circulate a DocuSign with the redline included. Can Redwood confirm you'll accept standard GreenLeaf signature workflow and that we can expect countersign by Redwood within 7 business days of DocuSign completion?

If so, we can move to signature and schedule a short ops walkthrough next week to validate deletion testing.

Best,
Luke Chen
Senior Director, Vendor Risk & Procurement, GreenLeaf Health
